courses.title: Japanese Foundations
courses.summary: Build a practical N5 foundation in sentence structure, particles, verbs and everyday vocabulary.
courses.description: A beginner path from Japanese word order through polite conversation. Lessons connect directly to the canonical grammar, dictionary and kanji knowledge systems.

lessons.title: Japanese sentence order
lessons.summary: Learn topic–comment structure and why the verb usually comes last.
lessons.content: Japanese commonly follows topic–object–verb order. The predicate closes the sentence and particles identify each phrase's role.

lessons.title: Core particles: は, が and を
lessons.summary: Distinguish topic, subject and direct object marking.
objectives: Use は to set a topic
Use が to identify a subject
Use を with a transitive verb
lessons.content: Particles follow a phrase and show its grammatical role. は frames the topic, が identifies a subject or focus, and を marks the direct object.

lessons.title: Polite verbs with ます
lessons.summary: Conjugate common verbs into polite present, negative and past forms.
objectives: Use ます and ません
Use ました and ませんでした
lessons.content: The ます family is the standard neutral-polite verb system. It attaches to the continuative stem and carries tense and polarity.

lessons.title: Everyday requests
lessons.summary: Make polite requests with 〜てください and ask permission with 〜てもいい.
lessons.content: The て-form connects verbs to request and permission expressions. Register and social direction affect which request is appropriate.

courses.title: JLPT N4 Grammar Path
courses.summary: Master conditionals, reasons, aspect and obligation for the JLPT N4 level.
courses.description: An intermediate-beginner course that contrasts easily confused N4 patterns using corpus examples and common-mistake diagnostics.

lessons.title: Reasons: から and ので
lessons.summary: Choose between subjective and objective ways to give a reason.
objectives: Use から for a subjective reason
Use ので for an objective explanation
Attach ので after nouns correctly
lessons.content: から readily supports requests and decisions. ので packages the reason as background information and sounds softer.

lessons.title: Conditionals: たら, ば and なら
lessons.titleJa: 条件形：たら・ば・なら
lessons.summary: Compare event, hypothetical and context-taking conditionals.
objectives: Use たら for completed conditions
Use なら to respond to known context
lessons.content: Japanese conditionals overlap but differ in time, speaker control and discourse context. This lesson compares them side by side.

lessons.title: Completion and preparation
lessons.summary: Contrast 〜てしまう, 〜ておく and 〜てみる.
lessons.content: Auxiliaries after the て-form change how an event is viewed: completed, prepared in advance, or attempted as an experience.

lessons.title: Obligation and permission
lessons.summary: Use must, must not and may expressions accurately.
objectives: Express obligation with なければならない
Prohibit with てはいけない
Grant permission with てもいい
lessons.content: Japanese obligation often uses a double-negative logic. Permission and prohibition share the て-form but differ in the following predicate.

courses.title: JLPT N3 Grammar Path
courses.summary: Develop control of change, inference, logical conclusions and formal relations.
courses.description: A bridge to intermediate Japanese with structured comparisons, authentic examples and links into related vocabulary and kanji.

lessons.title: Change and effort
lessons.summary: Contrast 〜ようになる and 〜ようにする.
objectives: Use potential forms with ようになる
lessons.content: ようになる describes what comes to be true; ようにする describes what someone deliberately tries to make true.

lessons.title: Decisions and outcomes
lessons.summary: Contrast personal decisions with outcomes imposed by circumstances.
objectives: Use ことにする for your decision
Use ことになる for an external outcome
lessons.content: The choice between する and なる encodes agency: who makes the decision and whether the result is under the speaker's control.

lessons.title: Evidence and expectation
lessons.summary: Compare らしい, はず and かもしれない.
lessons.content: These patterns locate a statement on an evidence and confidence scale, from possible to logically expected.

lessons.title: Formal relations and viewpoints
lessons.summary: Use について, にとって, に対して and として.
lessons.content: Compound particles package relations that English often expresses with about, for, toward and as.

courses.title: Kanji Connections
courses.summary: Learn kanji through radicals, components, readings and high-frequency vocabulary.
courses.description: A knowledge-graph course built around the Kanji Mind Tree. Each lesson moves from visual structure to readings and words.

lessons.title: Nature elements: 日, 月, 火 and 水
lessons.summary: Connect four elemental kanji to components, readings and common words.
lessons.content: Concrete pictographic kanji provide an accessible starting point for visual analysis and compound vocabulary.

lessons.title: People and actions: 人, 行 and 来
lessons.summary: Use readings and components to connect people with movement verbs.
objectives: Read 人 in native and Sino-Japanese words
Contrast 行く and 来る
lessons.content: Readings change by word. This lesson uses the dictionary and reverse component links to show recurring patterns.

lessons.title: The language family: 言, 話 and 語
lessons.summary: Trace the speech radical through words for saying, talking and language.
lessons.content: The 言 radical creates a visible family. Component and vocabulary links explain both similarity and distinction.

lessons.title: Study and work: 学, 勉 and 働
lessons.summary: Learn common kanji used in school, study and work contexts.
objectives: Connect 働く with the person component
lessons.content: Useful semantic fields create stronger memory cues than isolated character lists.

courses.title: Practical Conversation
courses.summary: Apply grammar and vocabulary to introductions, plans, requests and everyday problems.
courses.description: Scenario-based lessons that retrieve facts from the same dictionary and grammar knowledge used throughout NihongoBridge.

lessons.title: Introductions and identity
lessons.summary: Introduce yourself with appropriate polite forms.
objectives: Choose です and ます forms
lessons.content: A short introduction combines the polite copula, topic marking and formulaic social vocabulary.

lessons.title: Making plans together
lessons.summary: Invite someone, respond and settle a time and place.
lessons.content: Natural invitations are indirect. This lesson contrasts the invitation and volitional endings in a realistic exchange.

lessons.title: Requests and permission
lessons.summary: Ask for help and permission without sounding abrupt.
lessons.content: Request strength depends on relationship and context. Practice polite forms and their softer alternatives.

lessons.title: Explaining a problem
lessons.summary: Give reasons, describe completed mistakes and ask what to do.
objectives: Explain with ので or から
Express regret with てしまう
lessons.content: Problems require connected speech: describe what happened, explain why, and request an appropriate response.
